name: Operator Fatigue/Attention Levels
description: Human operators’ attentiveness and fatigue levels will dramatically affect their analysis time.  Fatigue leads to slower processing, misinterpretations, and ultimately, longer review times. This is *very* likely to be a significant contributor given the existing multimodal distribution.

name: Image Quality Variations (Lighting, Weather)
description: Changes in lighting conditions (sun glare, shadows, overcast) and weather (rain, fog, haze) significantly impact the quality of images, making them harder to analyze.  Poor image quality directly influences the time needed to resolve ambiguities and might trigger more complex operator analysis.

name: Operator Experience/Training
description: Operators with varying levels of experience and specific training will naturally exhibit different speeds and approaches to image analysis. More experienced operators may be quicker at identifying anomalies or require less detailed scrutiny.

name: Time of Day/Operational Phase
description: Operator alertness and cognitive performance varies throughout the day, and mission phase.  Analyzing images during peak operational hours (e.g., late morning) might lead to increased scrutiny and longer times compared to less active periods.

name: Task Complexity (Object Type, Scene Detail)
description: Images depicting more complex scenes or containing objects that are difficult to identify or differentiate will require longer analysis times, regardless of the analyst’s skill.  The subjective 'difficulty' of the task contributes to variation.

name: Onboard Classifier Confidence Levels
description: The UAV's classifier may output confidence scores. If the confidence is low, the operator is likely to spend more time scrutinizing the image, leading to longer analysis times. The multimodal distribution suggests that the onboard classifier's confidence is variable.

name: UAV Camera Calibration/Performance
description: Variations in camera calibration (focus, distortion) and sensor performance can introduce image artifacts that complicate analysis, especially for the onboard classifier.

name: Operator Preferences/Workflow
description: Operators might have differing preferences on how they approach image analysis. Some might prefer a more conservative approach (sending everything to the operator) while others are more comfortable with the onboard classifier.

name: Network Latency/Connectivity
description: Although not directly image analysis time, network latency could impact the responsiveness of the system and operator interaction, possibly leading to a perceived delay.  This could also contribute to frustration and slower operation.

name: Operator Mental State (Stress/Distraction)
description: Operator stress or distractions can significantly impact their ability to focus and analyze images efficiently.  This can be highly variable.

name: Image Resolution
description: Lower image resolution requires more detailed examination and therefore increased analysis time.  This interacts with image quality.

name: Operator Task Load
description: If the operator is simultaneously handling multiple tasks, their analysis time will be affected.

name: Waypoint Type
description: The type of the waypoint itself (e.g., densely populated area vs. open field) may influence the types of objects and scenes seen, and therefore the complexity of analysis needed.

name: Operator’s Familiarity with the Scene
description: If the operator is familiar with the area being imaged (e.g., has previous data), they may be quicker to identify relevant objects/anomalies.

name: System Load (UAV Processing)
description: The computational load on the UAV's onboard systems while performing image processing can introduce latency, indirectly affecting the operator’s decision-making.
